chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
title: Leaving Eckstine in September 1945 to study, and forming a trio
summary: Convinced he must stop and learn more, he leaves despite Eckstine's protest and forms a Nat Cole-style trio with Tommy Potter and Chester Brown.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: And Sarah was replaced by a girl named Ann Sawyer, a very fine vocalist. The last time I saw her, she had married and had a club in West Virginia. Ann Sawyer came in, and different guys were beginning to leave the band. So by this time, I was thoroughly convinced that I was in an entirely new and different atmosphere. My whole musical concept had changed 100 percent. And I was convinced that I needed to study and try to learn some more about what I was doing, and I realized that I couldn't do it traveling on the road.
So I went to Billy and I told him that I was going to

leave the band. He was quite disturbed. He said, "Whatever for? You're playing great, you're writing great" and the whole thing. I told him, "I really need to go home and study and learn." He said, "Man, you know enough. You should stay out here with the band." But I was convinced that I needed to know more.

So I quit the band and I came back to Washington. That was in September 1945. I came to Washington and formed a little trio. Incidentally, Tommy Potter left the band shortly after I did. When they came back, I formed this trio... Nat King Cole was at his peak then as far as the trio situation was concerned, and I liked the idea that the clubs were all using trios. There was a very good guitar player in Washington then whose name was Chester Brown. Chester and I had played together earlier in the Tommy Miles band. He was just one of those very talented guitarists, like so many musicians you meet that just got a little something extra in their sound and the way they play and everything.
